text: Composite armor is defined as having more than one layer of different materials or a matrix.
source_document: International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), 22 CFR Parts 120-130, amended through 2 October 2025 (KB 2/USA/ITAR.pdf)

text: Spaced armors are metallic or non-metallic armors that incorporate an air space or obliquity or discontinuous material path effects as part of the defeat mechanism.
source_document: International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), 22 CFR Parts 120-130, amended through 2 October 2025 (KB 2/USA/ITAR.pdf)

text: Reactive armor employs explosives, propellants, or other materials between plates for the purpose of enhancing plate motion during a ballistic event or otherwise defeating the penetrator.
source_document: International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), 22 CFR Parts 120-130, amended through 2 October 2025 (KB 2/USA/ITAR.pdf)

text: Electromagnetic armor (EMA) employs electricity to defeat threats such as shaped charges.
source_document: International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), 22 CFR Parts 120-130, amended through 2 October 2025 (KB 2/USA/ITAR.pdf)

text: Materials used in composite armor could include layers of metals, plastics, elastomers, fibers, glass, ceramics, ceramic-glass reinforced plastic laminates, encapsulated ceramics in a metallic or non-metallic matrix, functionally gradient ceramic-metal materials, or ceramic balls in a cast metal matrix.
source_document: International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), 22 CFR Parts 120-130, amended through 2 October 2025 (KB 2/USA/ITAR.pdf)

text: For this category, a material is considered transparent if it allows 75% or greater transmission of light, corrected for index of refraction, in the visible spectrum through a 1 mm thick nominal sample.

text: Metal laminate armors are two or more layers of metallic materials which are mechanically or adhesively bonded together to form an armor system.
source_document: International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), 22 CFR Parts 120-130, amended through 2 October 2025 (KB 2/USA/ITAR.pdf)

text: Em is the line-of-sight target mass effectiveness ratio and provides a measure of the tested armor's performance to that of rolled homogenous armor, where Em is defined as follows: ρRHA = density of MIL-A-12560 RHA (7.85 g/cm3) Po = Baseline Penetration of RHA (mm) Pr = Residual Line of Sight Penetration, either positive or negative (mm RHA equivalent) ADRHA = Line-of-Sight Areal Density of RHA (kg/m2) ADTARGET = Line-of-Sight Areal Density of Target (kg/m2) If witness plate is penetrated, Pr is the distance from the projectile to the front edge of the witness plate. If the target armor has no measurable penetration, Pr = 0, and the Em equation reduces to a ratio of ADRHA /ADTARGET.
source_document: International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), 22 CFR Parts 120-130, amended through 2 October 2025 (KB 2/USA/ITAR.pdf)
